essence: Zora is unforgettable not for any marvel but for the exact order of its streets, doors and windows, which the learned use as a scaffold for everything they must remember; forced to stay unchanged in order to be remembered, the real city wasted away and vanished.
textDetails: Lies beyond six rivers and three mountain ranges.
Nobody who has seen it can forget it, though not because it leaves some unusual image behind.
It is remembered point by point, in order: its streets, the houses lining them, the doors and windows of those houses.
Nothing in it has any particular beauty or rarity.
The secret lies in how the eye travels across forms that succeed each other like a musical score in which no single note may be altered or shifted.
A man who knows it by heart, when he cannot sleep at night, walks its streets in imagination.

The fixed order of that walk: copper clock, barber's striped awning, fountain with nine jets, astronomer's glass tower, melon vendor's kiosk (the Italian may specify watermelons; unverified), statue of the hermit and the lion, Turkish bath, cafe at the corner, alley leading to the harbour.
The city is like an armature, a honeycomb in Weaver's English (in the Italian an armature or grid of compartments), in whose cells each person can place what he wants to remember.
Things placed there: names of famous men, virtues, numbers, vegetable and mineral classifications, dates of battles, constellations, parts of speech.
Every idea can be tied to a point on the route by resemblance or by contrast, which then works as an instant memory cue.
Hence the most learned people in the world are the ones who have Zora by heart.
Marco set out to visit it in vain.
Compelled to remain immobile and unchanging so as to be easier to remember, Zora wasted away, came apart and disappeared, and the earth no longer remembers her.
visualConcept: A plain, pale city on a long floating plinth, laid out like a page of music: five long parallel streets form a staff, cross-alleys fall like bar lines, and rows of modest, identical houses rise and fall in a fixed rhythm with their doors and windows set like notes, nothing rare or beautiful in any single one (the staff plan is a design reading of Calvino's musical-score simile). It is night, the night of a man who cannot sleep, and a single lantern-bearer walks the city's unalterable itinerary: copper clock, barber's striped awning, fountain with nine jets, astronomer's glass tower, melon vendor's kiosk, statue of the hermit and the lion, Turkish bath, corner cafe, and the alley down to the harbour. Each landmark wakes as he reaches it, like a note being played, and sends a fine golden thread up to a honeycomb lattice floating above the city, whose cells hold small luminous emblems of stored knowledge: constellations, numerals, a leaf and a crystal for the vegetable and mineral classifications, a laurel for the virtues, crossed swords for battle dates, busts for famous men, little glyphs for the parts of speech. The lattice is the armature of memory and the city is its index; together they read at a glance as a memory palace. Yet the plinth's edges are quietly shedding dust: held motionless for the sake of being remembered, the earthly Zora is already crumbling. Far off, three mountain ranges stand in layered silhouette and six thin rivers glint across the dark plain between the viewer and the city, the distance that makes the visit futile.
layout: Plan convention: +X east, -Z north, y up. Rectangular plinth 40 x 26 (x by z), top at y=0, 1.0 thick, pale stone, floating over a dim plain at y=-6 crossed by 6 thin silver river ribbons (width 0.3-0.6) running roughly east-west in front of the plinth (+Z side, toward the camera); 3 mountain-range silhouettes as layered cut-out planes at distances 120, 160 and 200 in the fog. Staff: 5 streets running west to east (along x, length 34, width 1.4) at z = -8, -4, 0, 4, 8; cross-alleys (width 0.8) every 5.5 units like bar lines. Houses: about 420 instanced modules (width 0.9, depth 1.2) in continuous rows on both sides of each street, heights taken from one fixed repeating rhythm (1.0, 1.4, 1.8, 1.4, 1.0, 2.2, 1.4, 1.0), each facade a strict grid of one door plus 2-6 windows, white plaster and plain tiled roofs. Nine landmarks along a route that reads like a score, left to right along the top street, then down street by street: 1 copper clock tower (h 4.5, copper face r 0.5) at the west end of the north street; 2 barber's shop with a red-and-white striped awning; 3 small square with a round basin r 1.2 and 9 jets in a ring; 4 astronomer's octagonal glass tower (h 7, width 1.4, visible spiral stair, telescope on top); 5 melon kiosk with a heap of about 20 green striped melons; 6 statue on a 1.0 pedestal, a robed hermit with a lion lying at his feet (1.2 tall overall); 7 Turkish bath, a low block with one large dome (r 1.4) pierced by star-shaped skylights plus 4 small domes; 8 corner cafe with 6 small tables and chairs; 9 narrow alley (width 0.6) at the east end of the south street opening onto a small harbour basin (6 x 4) cut into the plinth, with 3 moored boats. Lattice: about 70 hexagonal cells (circumradius 1.6) as a flat honeycomb of gilt wire edges at y = 11-12, tilted 5 deg, each cell with a faint glass floor; about 40 cells carry an emblem (0.6-0.9 across) built from points and lines.
signatureMotion: 1) The insomniac's walk, a 54-second loop identical every time: the lantern-bearer moves along the fixed route, about 6 s per landmark; at each arrival the landmark wakes (clock hands tick, awning stirs, nine jets rise, the glass tower lights from within, melons glow under a lamp, the statue is lit, bath skylights sparkle, cafe lamps warm, the alley opens onto harbour lights) and a golden thread climbs to its lattice cell, whose emblem brightens. Lit landmarks stay lit like played notes until the loop ends and all darken together. 2) The score playhead: every 12 s a soft vertical bar of light sweeps west to east, and the windows it passes flash in an exact, unchanging pattern, street by street like staff lines; no randomness anywhere. 3) Quiet decay: a fine dust (about 200 particles) sifts continuously from the plinth edges and drifts down into the void.
interactionDescription: Leaves the remembered Zora for the real site, where the journey is in vain. The lattice dims and empties, the walker stops, and from the edges inward the houses lose height and break into dust that falls and drifts away over about 8 s, until only a bare plinth remains with faint foundation lines in the dust under cold moonlight. Toggling back rebuilds Zora from memory in itinerary order: the nine landmarks first, then the rows of houses rising like notes written onto the staff, and the lattice relights.
mood: Deep, clear night of insomnia: a high cold moon from the north-west, a sky crowded with stars (the constellations someone is memorising), the city chalk-pale and perfectly still, no wind, warm gold only at the landmarks and in the lattice, a cold glint of glass at the astronomer's tower. Exact, hushed, faintly melancholy.
caption: Across six rivers and over three mountain chains lies a city nobody forgets, although nothing in it is rare. Its streets, doors and windows follow one another like a score where no note may shift. Sleepless, the learned stroll it in their minds, from the copper clock past the barber's stripes and the nine-jetted fountain toward the harbour, filing a fact in every cell. Held so still for their sake, the real Zora has crumbled to dust.
motto: To be remembered exactly, a city must stop living.
camera: Elevated three-quarter view from the south, distance 46, elevation 40 deg, target (0, 4, 0), so the five streets run left to right across the frame like a staff and the honeycomb lattice floats in the upper third, with the river ribbons in the foreground. Slow lateral dolly of +/-6 units along x, following the walker's progress.
